newsitem.title: UK: BA uses Stansted for more UK cargo flights.
newsitem.headline: BA uses Stansted for more UK cargo flights.

text.p: British Airways said that because of pressure on landing and take-off slots, it has begun moving its ex-London cargo flights to Stansted from Gatwick.

Graham Bunsell, outsourcing manager of BA World Cargo, told Reuters that the switch, commencing from the beginning of this month, had followed the movement of an increasing number of BA passenger services to Gatwick from London Heathrow.
On March 17, BA transferred its routes to Argentina, Brazil, Colombia, Chile, Mexico and Venezuela to Gatwick from Heathrow.

Approval of a proposed link-up between BA and American Airlines is dependent, among other factors, of BA acceding to a demand by the British Office of Fair Trading to give up Heathrow slots to make way for new competition, industry analysts say.
That would mean more BA passenger flights having to move to Gatwick, displacing some of the carrier's services, particularly cargo flights, from the Sussex airport, they add.
"There has been a marked increase in pressure on BA slots at Gatwick. We have decided to start moving out of there before its slot situation becomes untenable," said Bunsell.
He added that from the beginning of this month, BA had moved a weekly London-Nairobi freighter service to Stansted from Gatwick using a 40-tonne capacity DC-8 freighter wet-leased from Intavia.
Wet-leasing covers the hire of both aircraft and crew.
Another similar weekly Gatwick-Nairobi DC-8 cargo charter service, operated by a DC-8-62F on wet-lease from Luxembourg-registered Cargolion, was also moved to Stansted from April1.
And at the same time, a weekly service to and from Nairobi and Johannesburg operated by a wet-leased Cargolion DC-8-62F was transferred to Stansted from Gatwick.

Cargo manager of BAA -owned and operated Stansted, Tony Astor, said that a three-times-weekly, 100-tonne capacity BA Boeing 747-200 freighter service now operated from Gatwick to Hong Kong would move to Stansted from next month.
This operated on a wet-lease basis for BA by U.S. carrier Atlas Air.

"And, once operating problems have been resolved, BA's planned new twice-weekly UK-Israel cargo service, using a Channel Express A300B4 freighter, wiull operate from Stansted and not Gatwick as BA originally planned," said Astor.
"Stansted is uncongested, has plenty of available runway slots and expects to handle even more BA freighter flights in the future," he said.
